What Are Our Powder Coating Services?

They are ten connected metal finishing services that take a part from rust, scale or old paint to a cured, tested finish. Some jobs need one step, others need several, and we combine them into a single order.

Powder coating itself is a dry powder sprayed by electrostatic spray and hardened by oven curing, which gives protective coatings that resist chips, fading and corrosion better than many liquid paints. Around that core sit the supporting coating services: surface preparation, blasting, colour work, stripping and recoating, plus specialist work for vehicles, wheels, buildings, volume orders and one-off pieces. That one-stop finishing approach keeps quality consistent and saves you managing several suppliers, each with its own schedule, standards and paperwork.
What We Can Coat: Size, Weight and Volume

Parts as long as 23 ft and as heavy as 6,000 lb fit our line, in quantities from a single piece to recurring batches. Metals include carbon steel and aluminum, structural steel, cast iron and galvanized steel.

How Our Powder Coating Services Work

Every order follows the same eight steps, from checking your drawing to packing the finished parts. The steps are fixed so results stay consistent, whether we handle one service for you or all of them.
Inspection & Spec Review

We check each part against your drawing, confirm the finish and mark every surface that must stay bare. We also agree which of our powder coating services the part needs, so nothing is added later without your approval.
Abrasive & Mobile Sandblasting
Blasting removes rust, mill scale and old coatings, in the shop or on site, leaving a clean profile the powder can grip.
Cleaning & Phosphate Pretreatment
Degreasing and pretreatment prepare the metal so the powder bonds firmly, then parts are rinsed and fully dried. Pretreatment also slows corrosion under the coating if the finish is ever damaged.
Masking & Plugging
Masking and plugging protect threads, mounting faces and contact points. Plugs and high-temperature tape come off after curing, leaving clean edges.
Electrostatic Powder Application
Charged powder wraps around edges and into corners for even coverage, the core of our service range. Film build is kept even so colour and gloss match across every part in a batch.
Oven Curing
Parts cure at 180–200 °C until the metal itself reaches temperature, so thick sections cure fully. Curing time follows the powder maker's data sheet, not guesswork.
Quality Inspection & DFT Check
Quality inspection covers film thickness, adhesion, colour and coverage before release. Results are recorded, so test reports can go out with any of our coating services on request.
Packaging & Shipping
Packaging and shipping protect finished faces, and the job ends with pickup or delivery. Finished faces are wrapped so they arrive exactly as they left inspection, the final step of every service.

blocks.text: An outside body, the Absolute Bureau of Certification, certifies our quality system, and we can send test reports with any order. See [powder coating quality assurance](/certification) for the full checks behind our powder coating services. Readings are taken where coatings fail first, on edges, welds and inside corners, not only on flat faces, and any part that misses a check is corrected before it leaves.

If you need readings for a supplier audit or a warranty file, ask when you order. We match the paperwork to your quality system, from a single summary to readings for each part, and keep the records so repeat orders for the same powder coating services can be checked against the first.

Powder Coating Services vs Wet Paint vs Galvanizing

Powder gives durable finishes in almost any colour, wet paint suits quick touch-ups and heat-sensitive parts, and galvanizing gives zinc protection with limited looks. The table compares all three at a glance.

For a deeper look, read [powder coating vs wet paint](/post/powder-coating-vs-wet-paint-toronto) and [powder coating vs galvanizing](/post/powder-coating-vs-galvanizing-corrosion-protection). Galvanized steel can also be powder coated when you want both zinc protection and colour.

Many customers combine methods, with zinc underneath for protection and powder on top for colour. Our coating services team can advise which route suits your part, its exposure and its budget before you commit.

What Affects Cost and Lead Time

Price and timing for powder coating services depend on part size, the prep needed, quantity, colour and masking. Standard orders leave two working days after drop-off, while oversized or complex jobs get their own written schedule with the quote.

Heavy rust or old coatings add blasting or stripping time, while batches of matching parts spread setup costs. Special colours and detailed masking add labour. We do not list prices here, because two similar parts can need different work. For typical ranges, read our guide to [powder coating cost](/post/how-much-does-powder-coating-cost-ontario), then ask for a written price on your own parts. Every service is priced job by job. If your deadline is fixed, say so with the request, and we will confirm in writing whether the date can be met before you book.
How to Get a Quote for Our Work

Send photos, sizes, quantity, metal and the finish you want for anything in our service range, and we come back with a written price, prep plan and timeline. You can also bring parts to our Milton shop, just off Hwy 401, Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM.
Use the online [powder coating quote](/get-a-quote) form, or phone (905) 876-7060.
Powder Coating Services FAQs

Short answer: one shop, one quote and one standard 48 hour turnaround for most orders. These five answers cover the pricing basis, timing, areas we serve, combined orders and order size; every service page answers its own questions.

blocks.a: By part size, prep, quantity, colour and masking. We price each order from photos and sizes, so you pay for the work your parts actually need, with no hidden extras added after the job is done.

blocks.q: What is your usual turnaround time?
blocks.a: Standard orders are ready in 48 hours from drop-off. Large or complex jobs get a written timeline before work starts.
Customers across the region send parts to our shop; see [powder coating service areas](/locations) for each city, with drive times, routes and drop-off details.

blocks.q: Can I combine several services in one order?
blocks.a: Yes. Combined orders, such as stripping, blasting and colour matching, are quoted together and run as one job.

blocks.q: Do you take one-off jobs as well as volume work?
blocks.a: Yes. All of our coating services are available for single parts and recurring batches alike, and both go through the same prep, curing and inspection as every other order.
